newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat futures end lower but off lows on rally.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat futures end lower but off lows on rally.

text.p: A late short-covering rally lifted KCBT hard red winter wheat futures off their lows, but they still ended lower on the day, traders said.
"A lot of guys got caught with their pants down on the short side and were in trouble when we hit (buy) stops at $4.41 to $4.42 (in KCBT December)," a trader said.
KCBT wheat was lower for most of the session on spillover pressure from CBOT corn and soybeans, which dropped sharply on USDA's quarterly stocks report released Monday.
The report showed U.S. corn and bean stocks at levels above analysts' average expectations.

Traders said that although the wheat number was bullish, wheat futures could not overcome the bearishness in corn and beans. USDA said wheat stocks as of Sept. 1 were at 1.724 billion bushels, below average estimates of 1.767 billion.
KCBT wheat closed 1/4 to seven cents per bushel lower, with Dec down 1/4 cent at $4.42
CIS sold one million Dec bushels and Benson-Quinn sold one million March. Refco bought 1.2 million Dec, traders said.
Spread trade was active, with General Mills bear spreading one million March/Dec at between 12-1/2 and 14-1/2 cents.
KCBT estimated Monday's volume at 33.52 million bushels, up from 24.340 million Friday.
